design_detail: Research letter (The Lancet 351:1784, one page): a non-randomized, single-group before-and-after drug-challenge study, filed as prospective-cohort, the nearest design the schema allows with ROBINS-I ('human-laboratory' is tied to RoB 2, which does not fit a non-randomized comparison; same filing as sc_boehrer_1993). Eight normally hydrated healthy men aged 22 to 32 each took 47.5 mg MDMA hydrochloride (Sigma; equivalent to 40 mg MDMA base) in a capsule with 200 mL water at 10:00 (study conditions); three of them acted as untreated controls on another occasion at least 2 weeks later (the figure legend calls this placebo). Blood was taken before and 30 minutes and 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 hours after: plasma MDMA by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, arginine vasopressin (AVP, the antidiuretic hormone) by radioimmunoassay, cortisol and sodium. Before-after comparisons by repeated-measures analysis of variance or paired t test, with one-tailed p values for AVP and sodium. Approved by the UK Home Office (for buying and giving MDMA) and the King's College London Ethics Committee. The text gives ranges and p values; geometric mean AVP and mean MDMA over 24 hours appear only in a small low-resolution figure.
can_establish: That in these 8 healthy men a single 40 mg oral dose of MDMA was followed within 1 to 2 hours by a rise in plasma vasopressin (range 1.14-1.88 pmol/L before, 2.46-9.16 pmol/L at 2 hours) and a fall in plasma sodium of 1 to 3 mmol/L in 7 of the 8, while cortisol did not change significantly.
cannot_establish: That MDMA rather than time of day, posture or fluid intake caused the change (the control occasions were 3 of the 8 men, later and unblinded, and were not compared statistically); what happens at the larger amounts people often take, with dancing, heat or heavy drinking; whether the hormone rise reduced urine output or explains difficulty urinating (urine was not measured); anything about women; or that illness from low blood sodium follows from this effect plus fluid intake (no fluid loading was studied).

sample.recruitment: Not described; eight healthy male volunteers (p. 1784, 2nd paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Normally hydrated healthy men aged 22 to 32; no other criteria stated.
sample.demographics: Men aged 22 to 32; no other characteristics, and no history of drug use, reported.
sample.attrition: None reported; whether every man gave every sample is not stated, although the 2-hour ranges and the sodium count cover all 8.
sample.selection_effects: Eight healthy young men at rest in a research setting; no women, no dancing, heat or fluid loading; earlier MDMA use not stated.

exposure.measurement: Drug given by the investigators: 47.5 mg MDMA hydrochloride (Sigma), equivalent to 40 mg base, in a capsule; plasma MDMA measured by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (p. 1784, 2nd paragraph).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: one oral dose of 40 mg MDMA base with 200 mL water at 10:00, samples to 24 hours. The authors call it a relatively small dose and state, without a source, that street ecstasy frequently contains more than 100 mg of MDMA (p. 1784, 4th paragraph).
exposure.polysubstance: Not reported; use of other drugs, alcohol, nicotine or caffeine before or during the session is not described.

comparison.controls: Each man's own pre-dose values; in addition, three of the eight served as untreated controls on an occasion at least 2 weeks after the MDMA session (figure legend: placebo, n = 3). Fixed order, no blinding described, and no statistical comparison between MDMA and control occasions.
comparison.matching: Within person (before and after). Whether the control occasions followed the same clock times is not stated.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Fluid and food intake, posture and activity during the 24 hours, which can affect vasopressin and sodium, are not reported beyond normal hydration and the 200 mL taken with the capsule.

outcomes.instruments: Plasma AVP by radioimmunoassay (method cited to a chapter by the last author, reference 3); plasma MDMA by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry; plasma cortisol and sodium, methods not stated (p. 1784, 2nd paragraph).
outcomes.validity_norms: Reference ranges are not given. The authors note that AVP's initial elimination half-life is about 6 minutes (reference 4), so single samples can miss short peaks.
outcomes.operationalization: AVP rise as the change from baseline (paired t test at 2 hours, one-tailed; repeated-measures analysis of variance across time points for the figure); sodium fall as baseline against 2 hours (paired t test, one-tailed); cortisol baseline against 2 hours.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None; one-tailed tests for AVP and sodium. Editors' count of 4: AVP, sodium, cortisol and the AVP-MDMA correlation.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not reported; the measures are laboratory assays.

analysis.effect_sizes: AVP: baseline range 1.14-1.88 pmol/L, at 2 hours 2.46-9.16 pmol/L (paired t test p = 0.006, one-tailed; editors' note: about 0.012 two-tailed); maximum between 1 and 2 hours. Sodium: ranges 139-145 mmol/L at baseline and 140-142 mmol/L at 2 hours; fall of 1 to 3 mmol/L in 7 of 8 men and a rise of 1 mmol/L in the eighth (paired t test p = 0.025, one-tailed; about 0.05 two-tailed, editors' note). Cortisol: mean 331.4 nmol/L (range 208.8-603.4) before and 377.2 nmol/L (268.4-583.3) at 2 hours, not significant (p > 0.05). AVP and MDMA concentrations not correlated (Spearman r = 0.2, p = 0.1). Read approximately from the low-resolution figure: geometric mean AVP after MDMA about 1.5 pmol/L before, about 3 at 1 hour, about 4 at 2 hours, about 2.8 at 4 hours and about 1.5 by 8 hours; on the 3 control occasions about 1.3 before and about 0.6 to 1 pmol/L from 1 to 8 hours; both about 1.75 at 24 hours; mean plasma MDMA about 45 micrograms per litre at 2 hours and 47 at 4 hours, falling to about 23 at 8 hours. No means with SDs, intervals or standardized effects are printed.
analysis.preregistration_detail: None mentioned; a one-page research letter.
analysis.selective_reporting: The text tests only the 2-hour time point for AVP, sodium and cortisol; the control occasions appear only as a line in the figure, with no numbers or test; the figure's asterisks refer to a repeated-measures analysis of variance whose statistics are not given.

interpretation_gap.results_show: In 8 healthy men, a single 40 mg dose of MDMA was followed by a rise in plasma vasopressin peaking at 1 to 2 hours (one-tailed p = 0.006 at 2 hours) and a fall in plasma sodium of 1 to 3 mmol/L in 7 of 8 (one-tailed p = 0.025), the lowest 2-hour value being 140 mmol/L; cortisol did not change significantly; vasopressin did not correlate with MDMA concentration; on 3 later untreated occasions vasopressin fell slightly.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The title says low-dose MDMA induces vasopressin secretion. The letter concludes that the hyponatraemic illness seen in some people who take ecstasy is likely linked to this effect, that with excessive fluid even a relatively small dose could cause symptoms, that the rise is not part of a generalised stress response because cortisol did not change significantly, and that MDMA-induced hyponatraemia results from a pharmacological effect compounded by excessive fluid intake rather than a rare idiosyncratic reaction (p. 1784, 4th paragraph). No fluid loading, urine output or illness was studied; the stress-response argument rests on a non-significant change in 8 men (cortisol mean 331.4 to 377.2 nmol/L); and the causal title rests on a before-after design whose 3 control occasions were not compared statistically. The closing message, that people who take ecstasy should avoid drinking fluid in excess of the body's requirements, and the statement that MDMA reduces thirst perception and impairs judgment, are not based on data from this study (5th paragraph).

timeline.event: Holden and Jackson: near-fatal hyponatraemic coma attributed to vasopressin over-secretion after ecstasy, the one earlier case with raised vasopressin cited by this letter (reference 2); not read.

Simmler, Hysek and Liechti: a study titled as showing sex differences in the effects of MDMA on plasma copeptin (a marker of vasopressin release) in healthy volunteers, as cited by Hysek et al. (2014); not read.

Hysek and colleagues: in 32 healthy volunteers given MDMA 125 mg in a placebo-controlled crossover study, plasma copeptin measured before and 1 and 2 hours after did not change significantly (no statistic printed; Figure 4B).

replication.where_it_stands: This letter on 8 men is the direct measurement of vasopressin after MDMA that later papers on MDMA-related low blood sodium cite (cards sc_campbell_2008 and sc_rosenson_2007 describe it second-hand). A larger placebo-controlled study measuring copeptin after 125 mg found no significant overall change (Hysek et al., 2014). Whether MDMA raises vasopressin enough to matter, in whom and at which amounts is not settled by these data.

funding.funder: Not reported; the letter thanks Peter Milligan for statistical advice.
funding.affiliations_note: Academic Department of Accident and Emergency Medicine, Imperial College School of Medicine, St Mary's Hospital, London (J A Henry); Drug Control Centre and Department of Pharmacy, King's College London; Department of Physiology, United Medical and Dental Schools, St Thomas's Hospital Campus, London. The vasopressin assay method is cited to a chapter by the last author (reference 3).

what_would_settle_it: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study in women and men, at doses in the range people take, with standardized fluid intake and repeated measurement of vasopressin or copeptin, plasma sodium and osmolality, urine volume and urine osmolality over the hours after the dose.

domains.note: Before-after design: changes in vasopressin and sodium with time of day, posture and fluid intake are controlled only by 3 later, unblinded, untreated occasions that were not compared statistically; fluid intake after the 200 mL is not reported.

domains.domain: Bias in selection of participants into the study
domains.note: Eight healthy men; recruitment and earlier drug use not described, though selection is unlikely to depend on the outcome.
Dose given and recorded by the investigators; plasma MDMA measured.

domains.domain: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domains.note: Not blinded (untreated controls in the text, though the figure legend says placebo); activity, food and fluids during the 24 hours are not described.
The 2-hour ranges and the sodium count cover all 8 men; completeness at other time points is not stated.
Laboratory assays (radioimmunoassay, mass spectrometry) are unlikely to be influenced by knowing the condition; AVP's short half-life makes single samples noisy but not biased.

domains.domain: Bias in selection of the reported result
domains.note: Ranges and one-tailed p values for the 2-hour time point only, chosen after the peak was seen; no comparison with the control occasions; the time course appears only in a figure without statistics.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: A small uncontrolled before-after experiment with objective measures. The direction of the vasopressin rise is plausible, but without a randomized, blinded comparison the change cannot be cleanly attributed to MDMA, the tests are one-tailed at a selected time point, and the clinical conclusions go beyond the data. It may be cited as: in 8 healthy men, plasma vasopressin rose within 1 to 2 hours of a single 40 mg dose of MDMA while plasma sodium fell slightly (by 1 to 3 mmol/L in 7 of 8). It should not be cited as showing that MDMA causes water retention or low blood sodium in people who use it, or as explaining difficulty urinating.

key_findings.finding: Design and sample: 8 normally hydrated healthy men aged 22 to 32 each took 47.5 mg MDMA hydrochloride (40 mg base) in a capsule with 200 mL water at 10:00; 3 of them acted as untreated controls at least 2 weeks later; blood before and at 30 minutes and 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 hours for MDMA, vasopressin (AVP), cortisol and sodium.

Vasopressin: plasma AVP peaked between 1 and 2 hours after the dose; the baseline range of 1.14-1.88 pmol/L rose at 2 hours to 2.46-9.16 pmol/L (paired t test p = 0.006, one-tailed), in contrast with a small decrease on the control occasions.
key_findings.note: One-tailed; two-tailed p would be about 0.012 (editors' calculation). The controls are 3 later, untreated occasions, not compared statistically.

key_findings.finding: Sodium: ranges 139-145 mmol/L before and 140-142 mmol/L at 2 hours; 7 of 8 men fell by 1 to 3 mmol/L and one rose by 1 mmol/L (paired t test p = 0.025, one-tailed); the authors call it a small fall.
key_findings.locator: Letter, 3rd paragraph (left column, continuing in the right column) and 4th paragraph (right column)

key_findings.finding: Cortisol: mean 331.4 nmol/L (range 208.8-603.4) before and 377.2 nmol/L (268.4-583.3) at 2 hours, a non-significant rise (p > 0.05).
key_findings.locator: Letter, 3rd paragraph (top of the right column)

key_findings.finding: AVP and MDMA concentrations were not correlated (Spearman r = 0.2, p = 0.1); the authors attribute this to AVP's initial elimination half-life of about 6 minutes against hours for MDMA.
key_findings.note: With 8 independent pairs, r = 0.2 would give p of about 0.6; p = 0.1 fits roughly 64 pooled samples from the 8 men (editors' calculation). How the correlation was computed is not stated.

key_findings.finding: Figure, in the editors' approximate reading of a low-resolution image: geometric mean AVP after MDMA rose from about 1.5 pmol/L to about 4 at 2 hours and was back near 1.5 by 8 hours; on the 3 control occasions it stayed between about 0.6 and 1 pmol/L from 1 to 8 hours; mean plasma MDMA was about 45 micrograms per litre at 2 hours and 47 at 4 hours.
key_findings.note: Approximate values read from a low-resolution figure (a 72-ppi bitmap, enlarged); asterisks for difference from baseline appear beside the AVP points at about 1, 2 and 4 hours.

key_findings.finding: Authors' conclusions: the rise in AVP with a small fall in sodium makes hyponatraemic illness after ecstasy likely to be linked to the drug's ability to stimulate AVP secretion; with excessive fluid intake even a relatively small dose could lead to symptoms; the rise is not part of a generalised stress response because cortisol did not change significantly; animal studies show that MDMA releases serotonin and that serotonergic pathways regulate AVP secretion.

Authors' closing message, not tested in this study: people who take ecstasy or similar drugs may be at risk of hyponatraemia and should avoid drinking fluid in excess of the body's requirements, which may be hard to judge because MDMA reduces thirst perception and impairs judgment.

Background cited: MDMA use had been associated with acute symptomatic hyponatraemia with inappropriate antidiuretic-hormone secretion (Maxwell and colleagues, 1993, reference 1), and raised AVP had been found in one case (Holden and Jackson, 1996, reference 2).
key_findings.locator: Letter, 1st paragraph (left column); references 1 and 2 (right column)

reporting_issues.issue: The text says three volunteers acted as untreated controls at least 2 weeks later, while the figure legend labels this condition placebo (n = 3); no placebo capsule, blinding or statistical comparison with the MDMA occasions is described.
reporting_issues.consequence: The control condition is smaller, later, unblinded and of unclear nature; the MDMA effect rests on before-after change.

reporting_issues.issue: The AVP and sodium tests are one-tailed (p = 0.006 and 0.025) and are given for the 2-hour time point only; two-tailed values would be about 0.012 and 0.05 (editors' calculation).
reporting_issues.consequence: The sodium change is borderline by conventional two-sided testing; neither result is corrected for the choice of time point.

reporting_issues.issue: The Spearman correlation between AVP and MDMA (r = 0.2, p = 0.1) cannot come from 8 independent pairs, which would give p of about 0.6; it probably pools repeated samples from the same men, which the letter does not say (editors' calculation).
reporting_issues.consequence: The correlation's p value is not interpretable as printed.

reporting_issues.issue: No means, SDs or intervals are given for AVP or sodium, only ranges; the time course and the control occasions appear only in a low-resolution figure, whose legend refers to a repeated-measures analysis of variance without statistics.
reporting_issues.consequence: The size of the effect and its uncertainty cannot be computed.

reporting_issues.issue: The statement that street ecstasy frequently contains more than 100 mg of MDMA has no source.

verification.source_read: PDF PDFs/MDMA/Henry_1998_MDMAVasopressin.pdf (version of record), p. 1784 (the whole letter; the page also carries the end of another letter); every number checked on the page rendered at 200 dpi, and the figure (a 72-ppi bitmap) cropped and enlarged from a 400-dpi rendering and read only approximately. No supplement.
